section_1.title: The Grand Introduction: The Most Beautiful Equation
section_1.content: Introduce Euler's formula e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x) and its special case e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Explain why it is considered 'the most beautiful'—it connects five fundamental mathematical constants (0, 1, e, i, π) that seem to have nothing to do with each other.
section_1.example: Visualizing a bridge connecting five separate islands, each named after a constant: The Island of Counting (1), The Island of Nothingness (0), The Island of Ratios (π), The Island of Growth (e), and The Island of Imagination (i).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane and the Secret of 'i'
section_2.content: Establish the 2D Coordinate system where the X-axis represents Real numbers and the Y-axis represents Imaginary numbers. Explain that multiplying by 'i' is geometrically equivalent to a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.
section_2.example: A character named 'Neo' stands at point (1,0) on a map. When Neo encounters the operator 'i', he doesn't move forward; he turns 90 degrees left to face the 'Imaginary North' (0, i).

section_3.title: The Engine of Growth: Understanding 'e'
section_3.content: Briefly review 'e' as the base of natural growth. Explain that in the real world, e^x represents continuous growth in one direction. However, when we introduce 'i' into the exponent, the growth direction is forced to be perpendicular to the current position.
section_3.example: Imagine a drone trying to fly away from the center (growth), but a crosswind (the 'i' factor) constantly pushes it sideways. This constant 'sideways push' forces the drone into a perfect circular path rather than a straight line.

section_4.title: The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation
section_4.content: Connect the 'sideways growth' to trigonometry. Show that e^(ix) represents a point on the unit circle at an angle of 'x' radians. Use animation to show that as 'x' increases, the point moves around the circle, with its position always defined by (cos x + i sin x).
section_4.example: A 'Point-Bot' starts at (1,0). As we feed it a value for 'x', it walks along the edge of a circular track. Its horizontal position is cos(x) and its vertical position is sin(x).

section_5.title: The Destination: Plugging in π
section_5.content: Now, substitute x with π. Explain that π radians is a 180-degree turn (half a circle). Calculate cos(π) and sin(π). Show that cos(π) = -1 and sin(π) = 0.
section_5.example: The 'Point-Bot' travels a distance of π (half the circumference). It ends up exactly on the opposite side of the starting point, landing on the Real Axis at -1.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Unity of Mathematics
section_6.content: Synthesize the result: e^(iπ) = -1. Rearrange to the standard form e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Summarize how exponential growth, circular geometry, and imaginary numbers are actually different perspectives of the same reality.
section_6.example: A final animation showing the 'Bridge' from Section 1 solidifying, as the five constants light up in sequence to complete a circuit, symbolizing the perfect harmony of the equation.

section_1.title: The Grand Introduction: The Most Beautiful Equation
section_1.content: Introduce Euler's formula e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x) and its special case e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Explain why it is considered 'the most beautiful'—it connects five fundamental mathematical constants (0, 1, e, i, π) that seem to have nothing to do with each other.
section_1.example: Visualizing a bridge connecting five separate islands, each named after a constant: The Island of Counting (1), The Island of Nothingness (0), The Island of Ratios (π), The Island of Growth (e), and The Island of Imagination (i).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane and the Secret of 'i'
section_2.content: Establish the 2D Coordinate system where the X-axis represents Real numbers and the Y-axis represents Imaginary numbers. Explain that multiplying by 'i' is geometrically equivalent to a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.
section_2.example: A character named 'Neo' stands at point (1,0) on a map. When Neo encounters the operator 'i', he doesn't move forward; he turns 90 degrees left to face the 'Imaginary North' (0, i).

section_3.title: The Engine of Growth: Understanding 'e'
section_3.content: Briefly review 'e' as the base of natural growth. Explain that in the real world, e^x represents continuous growth in one direction. However, when we introduce 'i' into the exponent, the growth direction is forced to be perpendicular to the current position.
section_3.example: Imagine a drone trying to fly away from the center (growth), but a crosswind (the 'i' factor) constantly pushes it sideways. This constant 'sideways push' forces the drone into a perfect circular path rather than a straight line.

section_4.title: The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation
section_4.content: Connect the 'sideways growth' to trigonometry. Show that e^(ix) represents a point on the unit circle at an angle of 'x' radians. Use animation to show that as 'x' increases, the point moves around the circle, with its position always defined by (cos x + i sin x).
section_4.example: A 'Point-Bot' starts at (1,0). As we feed it a value for 'x', it walks along the edge of a circular track. Its horizontal position is cos(x) and its vertical position is sin(x).

section_5.title: The Destination: Plugging in π
section_5.content: Now, substitute x with π. Explain that π radians is a 180-degree turn (half a circle). Calculate cos(π) and sin(π). Show that cos(π) = -1 and sin(π) = 0.
section_5.example: The 'Point-Bot' travels a distance of π (half the circumference). It ends up exactly on the opposite side of the starting point, landing on the Real Axis at -1.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Unity of Mathematics
section_6.content: Synthesize the result: e^(iπ) = -1. Rearrange to the standard form e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Summarize how exponential growth, circular geometry, and imaginary numbers are actually different perspectives of the same reality.
section_6.example: A final animation showing the 'Bridge' from Section 1 solidifying, as the five constants light up in sequence to complete a circuit, symbolizing the perfect harmony of the equation.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout(

        )
        
        # Define Colors

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_circle)

        # Add local axes for reference (subtle)
        axes = Axes(

        # Updater for moving point

        self.play(FadeIn(angle_arc), angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/3), run_time=2)

        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI/3), run_time=2)

            end=axes.c2p(0, np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value())),
            color=color_sin
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(sin_line))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        )

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN)

            arc.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Final Cleanup for section end
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

import numpy as np

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Titles and lecture lines
        title = "The Destination: Plugging in π"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's substitute x with the value of pi.",
            "A rotation of pi radians is a half-circle turn.",
            "The point moves from one side to the exact opposite.",
            "At this position, cosine is -1 and sine is 0.",
            "Thus, e^(i pi) equals negative one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FF7F"
        RED_PULSE = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's substitute x with the value of pi.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Complex Plane setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": BLUE_E}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=GRAY).move_to(axes.get_center())
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="Re", y_label="Im")
        
        # Identity label
        identity_label = MathTex("e^{i x} \\rightarrow e^{i \\pi}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(identity_label, 'A3')

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(labels), Create(circle), Write(identity_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A rotation of pi radians is a half-circle turn.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # The moving point
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        # The path (arc)
        arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=1.0, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=theta_tracker.get_value(), 
            color=YELLOW
        ).move_to(axes.get_center()))
        
        self.add(dot, arc)
        
        # Rotate halfway
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The point moves from one side to the exact opposite.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # At this position, cosine is -1 and sine is 0.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(SPRING_GREEN))
        
        cos_text = MathTex("\\cos(\\pi) = -1", color=SPRING_GREEN, font_size=32)
        sin_text = MathTex("\\sin(\\pi) = 0", color=SPRING_GREEN, font_size=32)
        
        self.place_at_grid(cos_text, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(sin_text, 'C5')
        
        self.play(Write(cos_text), Write(sin_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Thus, e^(i pi) equals negative one.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED_PULSE))
        
        # Highlight destination with red pulse
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.1, color=RED_PULSE, stroke_width=8).move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        final_eq = MathTex("e^{i \\pi} = -1", color=RED_PULSE, font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(final_eq, 'F4')

        self.play(
            pulse.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            Write(final_eq),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.remove(pulse)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.0  # Shifted right to avoid lecture text
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Complex Plane and the Secret of 'i'",
            [
                "The complex plane combines real and imaginary numbers.",
                "Multiplying by i creates a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.",
                "This turns linear movement into a change in direction."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # Create the Complex Plane (Axes)
        real_axis = Line(left=LEFT * 2.5, right=RIGHT * 2.5, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        real_label = Text("Real", font_size=18, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(real_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        imag_axis = Line(start=DOWN * 2.5, end=UP * 2.5, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=2)
        imag_label = Text("Imaginary", font_size=18, color="#FFFF00").next_to(imag_axis, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        complex_plane = VGroup(real_axis, imag_axis, real_label, imag_label)
        self.place_in_area(complex_plane, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(real_axis), Create(imag_axis), Write(real_label), Write(imag_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Place a small green dot (#00FF00) at (1,0)
        origin = complex_plane.get_center()
        unit_length = 1.5
        
        dot = Dot(point=origin + RIGHT * unit_length, color="#00FF00", radius=0.1)
        dot_label = MathTex("1", font_size=20, color="#00FF00").next_to(dot, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Animate the dot rotating 90 degrees CCW to (0, i) with cyan arc
        arc = Arc(
            radius=unit_length,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=PI/2,
            arc_center=origin,
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        
        target_pos = origin + UP * unit_length
        i_label = MathTex("i", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF").next_to(target_pos, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Rotate(dot, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin),
            Create(arc),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.play(Write(i_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN)
        )
        
        # Pulse the arc to emphasize the change in direction
        self.play(
            arc.animate.set_stroke(width=6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Final Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

    def construct(self):
        # Title and lecture lines for Section 3
        title_text = "The Engine of Growth: Understanding 'e'"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The constant 'e' represents the base of natural growth.",
            "Usually, growth happens in one continuous forward direction.",
            "But the exponent 'i' pushes growth in a perpendicular direction.",
            "This constant sideways push creates a circular path.",
            "Euler's formula describes growth that turns into rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors used in the animation
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FA9A"
        HOT_PINK = "#FF69B4"

        # Anchor point for the visualization (Center of the D3 grid area)
        center_point = self.grid["D3"]
        
        # Gold vector starting at the origin and growing outwards.
        growth_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 1.2, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        self.play(GrowArrow(growth_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        self.play(growth_vector.animate.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 2.0))
        self.wait(1)

            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SPRING_GREEN)
        )
        
        tip = growth_vector.get_end()
        perp_vector = Arrow(tip, tip + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        self.play(Create(perp_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Move highlight to fourth line and show circular path
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Setup for rotation animation using ValueTracker and Updaters
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        radius = 2.0
        
        # Redefine vectors to use updaters for smooth rotation
        rotating_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * radius, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        push_vector = Arrow(center_point + RIGHT * radius, center_point + RIGHT * radius + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        
        def update_rot_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0]) * radius)
            
        def update_push_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            start = rotating_vector.get_end()
            perp_dir = np.array([-np.sin(ang), np.cos(ang), 0]) # Always perpendicular
            m.put_start_and_end_on(start, start + perp_dir * 0.8)

        rotating_vector.add_updater(update_rot_vec)
        push_vector.add_updater(update_push_vec)
        
        # Traced path for the circular arc
        arc_path = TracedPath(rotating_vector.get_end, stroke_color=HOT_PINK, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.remove(growth_vector, perp_vector)
        self.add(rotating_vector, push_vector, arc_path)
        
        # Animate the first 90 degrees of rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI / 2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Move highlight to fifth line and complete the turn
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Animate to 180 degrees (half circle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

The Manim code for **Section 5: The Destination: Plugging in π** has been implemented. 

### Key Features:
- **Visual Anchor System**: All elements, including the complex plane, trig labels, and the final identity formula, are positioned using the mandatory 6x6 grid (`place_at_grid`, `place_in_area`).
- **Dynamic Animations**:
    - A white point travels along the unit circle from $0$ to $\pi$ radians using a `ValueTracker`.
    - A yellow arc follows the point to visualize the "half-circle turn".
    - Trig values ($\cos(\pi) = -1$, $\sin(\pi) = 0$) appear in **Spring Green** (#00FF7F) as the destination is reached.
    - A **Red Pulse** (#FF0000) highlights the final position $(-1, 0)$ as the identity $e^{i\pi} = -1$ is revealed.
- **Style Constraints**: Lecture lines are updated with matching colors at each stage, and all font sizes are optimized for readability.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Titles and lecture lines
        title = "The Destination: Plugging in π"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's substitute x with the value of pi.",
            "A rotation of pi radians is a half-circle turn.",
            "The point moves from one side to the exact opposite.",
            "At this position, cosine is -1 and sine is 0.",
            "Thus, e^(i pi) equals negative one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FF7F"
        RED_PULSE = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's substitute x with the value of pi.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Complex Plane setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": BLUE_E}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=GRAY).move_to(axes.get_center())
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="Re", y_label="Im")
        
        # Identity label
        identity_label = MathTex("e^{i x} \\rightarrow e^{i \\pi}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(identity_label, 'A3')

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(labels), Create(circle), Write(identity_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A rotation of pi radians is a half-circle turn.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # The moving point
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.cos(theta_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(theta_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        # The path (arc)
        arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=1.0, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=theta_tracker.get_value(), 
            color=YELLOW
        ).move_to(axes.get_center()))
        
        self.add(dot, arc)
        
        # Rotate halfway
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The point moves from one side to the exact opposite.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # At this position, cosine is -1 and sine is 0.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(SPRING_GREEN))
        
        cos_text = MathTex("\\cos(\\pi) = -1", color=SPRING_GREEN, font_size=32)
        sin_text = MathTex("\\sin(\\pi) = 0", color=SPRING_GREEN, font_size=32)
        
        self.place_at_grid(cos_text, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(sin_text, 'C5')
        
        self.play(Write(cos_text), Write(sin_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Thus, e^(i pi) equals negative one.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED_PULSE))
        
        # Highlight destination with red pulse
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.1, color=RED_PULSE, stroke_width=8).move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        final_eq = MathTex("e^{i \\pi} = -1", color=RED_PULSE, font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(final_eq, 'F4')

        self.play(
            pulse.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            Write(final_eq),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.remove(pulse)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and lecture lines for Section 3
        title_text = "The Engine of Growth: Understanding 'e'"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The constant 'e' represents the base of natural growth.",
            "Usually, growth happens in one continuous forward direction.",
            "But the exponent 'i' pushes growth in a perpendicular direction.",
            "This constant sideways push creates a circular path.",
            "Euler's formula describes growth that turns into rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors used in the animation
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FA9A"
        HOT_PINK = "#FF69B4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line and show growth vector
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        # Anchor point for the visualization (Center of the D3 grid area)
        center_point = self.grid["D3"]
        
        # Gold vector starting at the origin and growing outwards.
        growth_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 1.2, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        self.play(GrowArrow(growth_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Move highlight to second line and show more growth
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        self.play(growth_vector.animate.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 2.0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Move highlight to third line and introduce perpendicular push
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SPRING_GREEN)
        )
        
        tip = growth_vector.get_end()
        perp_vector = Arrow(tip, tip + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        self.play(Create(perp_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Move highlight to fourth line and show circular path
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Setup for rotation animation using ValueTracker and Updaters
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        radius = 2.0
        
        # Redefine vectors to use updaters for smooth rotation
        rotating_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * radius, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        push_vector = Arrow(center_point + RIGHT * radius, center_point + RIGHT * radius + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        
        def update_rot_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0]) * radius)
            
        def update_push_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            start = rotating_vector.get_end()
            perp_dir = np.array([-np.sin(ang), np.cos(ang), 0]) # Always perpendicular
            m.put_start_and_end_on(start, start + perp_dir * 0.8)

        rotating_vector.add_updater(update_rot_vec)
        push_vector.add_updater(update_push_vec)
        
        # Traced path for the circular arc
        arc_path = TracedPath(rotating_vector.get_end, stroke_color=HOT_PINK, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.remove(growth_vector, perp_vector)
        self.add(rotating_vector, push_vector, arc_path)
        
        # Animate the first 90 degrees of rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI / 2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Move highlight to fifth line and complete the turn
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Animate to 180 degrees (half circle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Unity of Mathematics", [
            "We can rearrange this as e^(i pi) plus 1 equals 0.",
            "Growth, geometry, and imagination are now perfectly unified.",
            "This simple identity reveals the deep harmony of math."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Transform the equation e^{iπ} = -1 into the standard form e^{iπ} + 1 = 0.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Initial equation: e^{i\pi} = -1
        # Splitting into substrings for TransformMatchingTex
        eq1 = MathTex("e^{i\\pi}", "=", "-1", font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(eq1, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=2.0)
        
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Target equation: e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0
        eq2 = MathTex("e^{i\\pi}", "+1", "=", "0", font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(eq2, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=2.0)
        
        # Perform the rearrangement transformation
        self.play(TransformMatchingTex(eq1, eq2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight each of the five constants with distinct glowing colors (#FFD700, #ADFF2F, #00FFFF, #FF69B4, #FFFFFF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define granular equation for precise highlighting of constants: e, i, pi, 1, 0
        # Formula: e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0
        # Index breakdown for MathTex split:
        # 0:e, 1:^{, 2:i, 3:\pi, 4:}, 5:+, 6:1, 7:=, 8:0
        eq2_granular = MathTex(
            "e",          # 0
            "^{",         # 1
            "i",          # 2
            "\\pi",       # 3
            "}",          # 4
            "+",          # 5
            "1",          # 6
            "=",          # 7
            "0",          # 8
            font_size=48
        )
        self.place_in_area(eq2_granular, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=2.0)
        
        # Replace the previous eq2 with the granular version for coloring
        self.remove(eq2)
        self.add(eq2_granular)
        
        # Constants indices: e(0), i(2), pi(3), 1(6), 0(8)
        const_indices = [0, 2, 3, 6, 8]
        const_colors = ["#FFD700", "#ADFF2F", "#00FFFF", "#FF69B4", "#FFFFFF"]
        
        # Sequential highlighting with a flash effect to simulate "glowing"
        for idx, color in zip(const_indices, const_colors):
            self.play(
                eq2_granular[idx].animate.set_color(color),
                Flash(eq2_granular[idx], color=color, flash_radius=0.3, line_length=0.15),
                run_time=0.8
            )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a final khaki circle (#F0E68C) connecting all five constants to symbolize mathematical unity.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a circle that surrounds the whole identity to show unity
        unity_circle = Circle(color="#F0E68C", stroke_width=4)
        unity_circle.surround(eq2_granular, buffer_factor=1.4)
        
        self.play(Create(unity_circle), run_time=2)
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation",
            [
                "We start at the point (1, 0) on the circle.",
                "The term e^(ix) tracks a point moving along this circle.",
                "The angle 'x' determines how far the point travels.",
                "Its horizontal position is defined by the cosine of x.",
                "Its vertical position is defined by the sine of x."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define Colors
        color_circle = "#87CEEB" # sky-blue
        color_point = "#FFFFFF"  # white
        color_cos = "#FFA500"    # orange
        color_sin = "#FF4500"    # orange-red
        color_angle = "#FFFFE0"  # light yellow
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_circle)
        
        # Create a circle on the right side
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_circle)
        self.place_in_area(unit_circle, "B2", "E5")
        circle_center = unit_circle.get_center()
        
        # Add local axes for reference (subtle)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            x_length=3.0, # 1.5 radius * 2
            y_length=3.0,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_D, "include_tip": False}
        ).move_to(circle_center)
        
        # Point at (1,0)
        moving_point = Dot(unit_circle.point_at_angle(0), color=color_point)
        
        self.play(Create(unit_circle), Create(axes), FadeIn(moving_point))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_point)
        equation = MathTex("e^{ix}", "=", "\\cos(x)", "+", "i", "\\sin(x)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_angle)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_arc():
            val = angle_tracker.get_value()
            if val <= 0.01: return VectorizedPoint(location=circle_center)
            return Arc(
                radius=0.4,
                start_angle=0,
                angle=val,
                arc_center=circle_center,
                color=color_angle
            )
        angle_arc = always_redraw(get_arc)
        
        moving_point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            unit_circle.point_at_angle(angle_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(angle_arc), angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/3), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(color_cos)
        equation[2].set_color(color_cos)
        
        cos_line = DashedLine(color=color_cos)
        cos_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            moving_point.get_center(),
            circle_center + np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0, 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(cos_line))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI/3), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_sin)
        equation[5].set_color(color_sin)
        
        sin_line = DashedLine(color=color_sin)
        sin_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            moving_point.get_center(),
            circle_center + np.array([0, 1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(sin_line))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Grand Introduction: The Most Beautiful Equation
section_1.content: Introduce Euler's formula e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x) and its special case e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Explain why it is considered 'the most beautiful'—it connects five fundamental mathematical constants (0, 1, e, i, π) that seem to have nothing to do with each other.
section_1.example: Visualizing a bridge connecting five separate islands, each named after a constant: The Island of Counting (1), The Island of Nothingness (0), The Island of Ratios (π), The Island of Growth (e), and The Island of Imagination (i).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane and the Secret of 'i'
section_2.content: Establish the 2D Coordinate system where the X-axis represents Real numbers and the Y-axis represents Imaginary numbers. Explain that multiplying by 'i' is geometrically equivalent to a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation.
section_2.example: A character named 'Neo' stands at point (1,0) on a map. When Neo encounters the operator 'i', he doesn't move forward; he turns 90 degrees left to face the 'Imaginary North' (0, i).

section_3.title: The Engine of Growth: Understanding 'e'
section_3.content: Briefly review 'e' as the base of natural growth. Explain that in the real world, e^x represents continuous growth in one direction. However, when we introduce 'i' into the exponent, the growth direction is forced to be perpendicular to the current position.
section_3.example: Imagine a drone trying to fly away from the center (growth), but a crosswind (the 'i' factor) constantly pushes it sideways. This constant 'sideways push' forces the drone into a perfect circular path rather than a straight line.

section_4.title: The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation
section_4.content: Connect the 'sideways growth' to trigonometry. Show that e^(ix) represents a point on the unit circle at an angle of 'x' radians. Use animation to show that as 'x' increases, the point moves around the circle, with its position always defined by (cos x + i sin x).
section_4.example: A 'Point-Bot' starts at (1,0). As we feed it a value for 'x', it walks along the edge of a circular track. Its horizontal position is cos(x) and its vertical position is sin(x).

section_5.title: The Destination: Plugging in π
section_5.content: Now, substitute x with π. Explain that π radians is a 180-degree turn (half a circle). Calculate cos(π) and sin(π). Show that cos(π) = -1 and sin(π) = 0.
section_5.example: The 'Point-Bot' travels a distance of π (half the circumference). It ends up exactly on the opposite side of the starting point, landing on the Real Axis at -1.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Unity of Mathematics
section_6.content: Synthesize the result: e^(iπ) = -1. Rearrange to the standard form e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Summarize how exponential growth, circular geometry, and imaginary numbers are actually different perspectives of the same reality.
section_6.example: A final animation showing the 'Bridge' from Section 1 solidifying, as the five constants light up in sequence to complete a circuit, symbolizing the perfect harmony of the equation.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation",
            [
                "We start at the point (1, 0) on the circle.",
                "The term e^(ix) tracks a point moving along this circle.",
                "The angle 'x' determines how far the point travels.",
                "Its horizontal position is defined by the cosine of x.",
                "Its vertical position is defined by the sine of x."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define Colors
        color_circle = "#87CEEB" # sky-blue
        color_point = "#FFFFFF"  # white
        color_cos = "#FFA500"    # orange
        color_sin = "#FF4500"    # orange-red
        color_angle = "#FFFFE0"  # light yellow
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_circle)
        
        # Create a circle on the right side
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_circle)
        self.place_in_area(unit_circle, "B2", "E5")
        circle_center = unit_circle.get_center()
        
        # Add local axes for reference (subtle)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            x_length=3.0, 
            y_length=3.0,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_D, "include_tip": False}
        ).move_to(circle_center)
        
        # Point at (1,0)
        moving_point = Dot(unit_circle.point_at_angle(0), color=color_point)
        
        self.play(Create(unit_circle), Create(axes), FadeIn(moving_point))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_point)
        # Using VGroup of Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex' 
        # while maintaining indexing compatibility for color changes.
        equation = VGroup(
            Text("e^ix", font_size=36),
            Text("=", font_size=36),
            Text("cos(x)", font_size=36),
            Text("+", font_size=36),
            Text("i", font_size=36),

        lecture_lines = [
            "The constant 'e' represents the base of natural growth.",
            "Usually, growth happens in one continuous forward direction.",
            "But the exponent 'i' pushes growth in a perpendicular direction.",
            "This constant sideways push creates a circular path.",
            "Euler's formula describes growth that turns into rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors used in the animation
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FA9A"
        HOT_PINK = "#FF69B4"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line and show growth vector
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        # Anchor point for the visualization (Center of the D3 grid area)
        center_point = self.grid["D3"]
        
        # Gold vector starting at the origin and growing outwards.
        growth_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 1.2, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        self.play(GrowArrow(growth_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Move highlight to second line and show more growth
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        self.play(growth_vector.animate.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * 2.0))
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SPRING_GREEN)
        )
        
        tip = growth_vector.get_end()
        perp_vector = Arrow(tip, tip + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        self.play(Create(perp_vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Setup for rotation animation using ValueTracker and Updaters
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        radius = 2.0
        
        # Redefine vectors to use updaters for smooth rotation
        rotating_vector = Arrow(center_point, center_point + RIGHT * radius, buff=0, color=GOLD)
        push_vector = Arrow(center_point + RIGHT * radius, center_point + RIGHT * radius + UP * 0.8, buff=0, color=SPRING_GREEN)
        
        def update_rot_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, center_point + np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0]) * radius)
            
        def update_push_vec(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            start = rotating_vector.get_end()
            perp_dir = np.array([-np.sin(ang), np.cos(ang), 0]) # Always perpendicular
            m.put_start_and_end_on(start, start + perp_dir * 0.8)

        rotating_vector.add_updater(update_rot_vec)
        push_vector.add_updater(update_push_vec)
        
        # Traced path for the circular arc
        arc_path = TracedPath(rotating_vector.get_end, stroke_color=HOT_PINK, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.remove(growth_vector, perp_vector)
        self.add(rotating_vector, push_vector, arc_path)
        
        # Animate the first 90 degrees of rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI / 2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HOT_PINK)
        )
        
        # Animate to 180 degrees (half circle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Titles and lecture lines from storyboard
        title = "The Destination: Plugging in pi"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Plugging in pi creates a half-turn around the circle.",
            "At this point, the value is exactly negative one.",
            "We have reached the opposite side of our start."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        SPRING_GREEN = "#00FF7F"
        BRIGHT_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # The path (arc)
        arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=1.0, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=theta_tracker.get_value(), 
            color=YELLOW
        ).move_to(axes.get_center()))
        
        self.add(dot, arc)

        self.play(Write(cos_text), Write(sin_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We have reached the opposite side of our start.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BRIGHT_WHITE))
        
        final_eq = Text("e^(i*pi) = -1", color=BRIGHT_WHITE, font_size=32)
        # Apply Issue Fix for positioning
        self.place_in_area(final_eq, 'F3', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Box for finalized equation
        box = SurroundingRectangle(final_eq, color=BRIGHT_WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(formula_sub),
            FadeOut(cos_text),
            FadeOut(sin_text),
            Write(final_eq),
            Create(box)
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "The term e to the i x tracks rotation.",
            "Its position is defined by cosine and sine values.",
            "This formula shows how exponents and circles are related."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Formula in Motion: e^(ix) as a Rotation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard
        color_circle = "#808080"  # Grey
        color_point = "#FFFF00"   # Yellow
        color_cos = "#00FF00"      # Green
        color_sin = "#FF0000"      # Red
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_point)
        
        # Grey unit circle (#808080)
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_circle)
        self.place_in_area(unit_circle, "B2", "E5")
        center = unit_circle.get_center()
        
        # Faint axes for context
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2],
            x_length=3.0,
            y_length=3.0,
            axis_config={"color": GREY, "stroke_width": 1},
            tips=False
        ).move_to(center)
        
        # Yellow point (#FFFF00) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg]
        point_asset = SVGMobject("/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg")
        point_asset.set_color(color_point).scale(0.15)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Update point position based on angle
        point_asset.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            center + np.array([
                1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()),
                1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()),
                0
            ])
        ))
        
        self.add(axes)
        self.play(Create(unit_circle))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_asset))
        # Start rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/4), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_cos)
        
        # Projections
        # Horizontal 'cos(x)' in green on X-axis
        cos_line = Line(center, center, color=color_cos, stroke_width=6)
        # Vertical 'i sin(x)' in red on Y-axis
        sin_line = Line(center, center, color=color_sin, stroke_width=6)
        
        cos_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            center,
            center + np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0, 0])
        ))
        
        sin_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            center,
            center + np.array([0, 1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        # Connector dashed lines from point to axes
        dashed_h = DashedLine(color=GRAY_C, stroke_width=2)
        dashed_v = DashedLine(color=GRAY_C, stroke_width=2)
        
        dashed_h.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            point_asset.get_center(),
            center + np.array([0, 1.5 * np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        dashed_v.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            point_asset.get_center(),
            center + np.array([1.5 * np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0, 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(cos_line), Create(sin_line), Create(dashed_h), Create(dashed_v))
        # Continue rotation to show components updating
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(3*PI/4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Display e^{ix} = cos(x) + i sin(x)
        # Using MathTex with colored parts
        equation = MathTex("e^{ix}", "=", "\\cos(x)", "+", "i\\sin(x)", font_size=40)
        equation[2].set_color(color_cos) # cos(x)
        equation[4].set_color(color_sin) # i sin(x)
        
        # Resolve Issue 30/31: Align equation in A2-A5, scale 0.8
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        # Complete full circle rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2*PI), run_time=3.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)
